newsitem.title: FRANCE: French feed producers ready to label gene maize.
newsitem.headline: French feed producers ready to label gene maize.

text.p: French animal feed manufacturers said on Wednesday they were ready to start labelling products containing genetically modified maize, after the European Union approved imports of the grain.
Animal feed is produced mainly from locally grown maize in France, but the country's large feed industry also imports some 150,000 tonnes of corn gluten feed which is derived from maize.
"We are not at all hostile to the idea of making clear whenever genetically altered maize is involved," Paul Hervieu of the French animal feed association told Reuters.
"We will ask our members to show on labels when they are using maize or its by-products," he said.
The European Commission earlier approved the use in Europe of genetically modified maize grown in the United States but said it would seek improved labelling of gene-altered foods.
Swiss chemical giant Ciba-Geigy which developed the genetically modified maize has welcomed the EU's decision and has stated its readiness to cooperate on labelling.
Feed manufacturers are still reeling from bad publicity over the crisis surrounding mad cow disease, thought to have been caused by suspect feed containing ground-up animal parts.
Worries about a new consumer backlash are likely to make manufacturers even more determined not to lose points with the public over genetic tampering, food analysts said.
Hervieu agreed mad cow disease had made producers nervous.
"As we are just coming out of the mad cow crisis, there is a certain amount of apprehension about this sort of phenomenon, especially in view of statements that have been made," he said.
Environmentalists oppose gene-modified maize and similar experiments with soybeans as a health risk and are stepping up a campaign to build up opposition from the consumer.

Other grain processors have said labelling products made from gene-modified maize, which represents less than one percent of the U.S. maize or corn crop, is difficult because the raw commodity is sold in bulk and cannot be easily segregated.

The European Union imports two to three million tonnes of maize a year, mostly from the United States, and also buys five million tonnes of corn gluten, an alternative feedstuff. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5146
